scenarios.name: Cluster Formation and Leader Election
scenarios.description: Validates that a multi-node cluster forms correctly and elects a leader within specified time constraints

steps.description: Initialize and start the first node of a 3-node cluster
steps.context: Node should load cluster configuration and start in follower state waiting for election timeout

steps.description: Initialize and start the second node in the 3-node cluster
steps.context: Second node should discover first node via configured membership and initiate election

steps.description: Initialize and start the third node to complete the 3-node cluster
steps.context: Third node should join the existing cluster after leader election completes

steps.description: Check that all nodes are in the cluster and one node is leader
steps.context: Cluster status endpoint should show 3 healthy nodes with one identified as leader

test_cases.input: Start 3-node cluster and query status endpoint
test_cases.expected: Cluster status shows 3 nodes with one leader elected within 5 seconds

test_cases.input: Measure time from node 2 startup to leader election completion
test_cases.expected: Leader election completes within 500ms of node 2 startup

test_cases.input: Verify follower nodes do not accept write requests
test_cases.expected: SET commands sent to follower nodes return redirect to leader or error

test_cases.input: Verify all followers maintain leadership awareness
test_cases.expected: All follower nodes correctly identify the leader node ID

scenarios.name: Write Operation Replication with Majority Consensus
scenarios.description: Validates that write operations are replicated to a majority of nodes before acknowledgment and that data consistency is maintained

steps.description: Send a memcached SET command to store a key-value pair
steps.context: SET key1 0 0 5\r\nvalue1\r\n

steps.description: Client should receive STORED acknowledgment only after majority replication
steps.context: Leader must receive acknowledgment from at least one follower before responding STORED

steps.description: Query all follower nodes to confirm data replication
steps.context: GET key1 on all followers should return the stored value

steps.description: Confirm Raft log entries are persisted across node restarts
steps.context: Restart leader and verify committed entries are preserved

test_cases.input: SET command with data 'test_value_123' on key 'user_456'
test_cases.expected: Returns STORED after replication to at least 2 of 3 nodes; data readable from all nodes

test_cases.input: Measure write latency for consensus acknowledgment
test_cases.expected: Latency below 10ms in same datacenter environment with RTT < 5ms

test_cases.input: Verify write fails when majority unavailable (2 of 3 nodes down)
test_cases.expected: Write operations timeout or return error; no STORED response received

test_cases.input: Test multiple concurrent writes to leader
test_cases.expected: All writes acknowledged in correct order; no data loss or corruption

test_cases.input: Write 1000 sequential key-value pairs and verify all persist after restart
test_cases.expected: All 1000 key-value pairs remain accessible after all nodes restart

scenarios.name: Automatic Leader Failover
scenarios.description: Validates that cluster automatically elects a new leader when the existing leader fails and maintains consistency during failover

steps.action: Establish healthy 3-node cluster with active leader
steps.description: Start 3 nodes and wait for leader election; confirm leader identity
steps.context: All nodes healthy and leader sending heartbeats every election timeout/10

steps.action: Issue a write operation and wait for acknowledgment
steps.description: Send SET command for key 'test_key_failover' with value 'before_failover'
steps.context: Write should be replicated to majority and acknowledged before proceeding

steps.description: Kill the leader node process or disconnect network
steps.context: Remaining nodes should detect missed heartbeats after election timeout

steps.description: Monitor remaining nodes for leader election completion
steps.context: One of the followers should become candidate and win election after timeout

steps.description: Send new write and verify previous data persists
steps.context: New leader should accept writes; data from failed leader should be accessible

test_cases.input: Kill leader in 3-node cluster and measure time to new leader election
test_cases.expected: New leader elected within 500ms; client writes succeed within 600ms total time

test_cases.input: Verify no data loss after leader failure
test_cases.expected: GET for key written before failure returns correct value from new leader

test_cases.input: Test write operations during failover window
test_cases.expected: Client receives appropriate error or timeout; writes succeeding before leader failure remain committed

test_cases.input: Test 5-node cluster survives 2 node failures
test_cases.expected: Cluster remains available with 3 nodes; can continue accepting writes

test_cases.input: Recover original leader and observe it joins as follower
test_cases.expected: Original leader recovers automatically, joins cluster as follower, and catches up on missed entries

test_cases.input: Verify split-brain prevention during network partition scenario
test_cases.expected: Network partition does not result in multiple leaders; minority partition stops accepting writes

scenarios.name: Follower Reads for Eventually-Consistent Queries
scenarios.description: Validates that follower nodes can serve read requests with eventual consistency guarantees and replication lag bounds

steps.description: Execute SET command for test data on leader
steps.context: SET read_test_key 0 0 8\r\ntest_value\r\n

steps.description: Send GET command to a follower node
steps.context: Follower should respond with data if replication lag is acceptable

steps.description: Monitor lag between leader and followers over time
steps.context: Follower should catch up quickly after write

test_cases.input: Execute GET on follower node immediately after write to leader
test_cases.expected: Follower returns correct value after replication completes (< 100ms lag)

test_cases.input: Load test with 80% reads on followers, 20% writes on leader
test_cases.expected: Follower read throughput scales linearly; replication lag remains < 100ms

test_cases.input: Verify follower handles non-existent keys correctly
test_cases.expected: GET for non-existent key returns 'END' as per memcached protocol

test_cases.input: Test multiple GET keys on follower
test_cases.expected: Follower correctly handles get with multiple keys (get key1 key2 key3)

scenarios.name: Snapshot-Based Node Recovery
scenarios.description: Validates that new nodes joining the cluster or recovering nodes receive efficient state transfer via snapshots rather than full log replay

steps.description: Write large number of key-value pairs to populate database
steps.context: Write 100,000+ key-value pairs to create substantial log history

steps.description: Start new node with cluster configuration pointing to existing cluster
steps.context: New node should join as follower and request state transfer

steps.description: Verify leader sends snapshot instead of replaying full log
steps.context: Log size should exceed snapshot threshold to trigger optimization

steps.action: Verify node synchronizes to current state
steps.description: Confirm new node catches up and can serve requests
steps.context: New node should become healthy follower after state transfer

test_cases.input: Add new node to cluster with 50,000 existing log entries
test_cases.expected: Leader sends snapshot; node syncs without replaying 50,000 entries; recovery completes within reasonable time (<30 seconds)

test_cases.input: Verify snapshot includes complete state
test_cases.expected: All key-value pairs present and queryable on new node after sync

test_cases.input: Test snapshot during concurrent writes
test_cases.expected: Snapshot includes consistent point-in-time state; new node catches up on subsequent writes after joining

test_cases.input: Verify snapshot cleanup prevents unbounded log growth
test_cases.expected: Raft log compacted periodically; disk usage remains stable over time

scenarios.name: Cluster Health and Status Monitoring
scenarios.description: Validates that cluster provides status endpoints showing node health, leader identity, replication lag, and log positions

steps.description: Send INFO command or HTTP request to status endpoint
steps.context: Endpoint should return cluster state information

steps.description: Status should identify which node is the current leader
steps.context: Clients need to know leader for write operations

steps.description: Check that replication lag is visible for each follower
steps.context: Database administrators monitor catch-up progress

test_cases.input: Call cluster status endpoint on any node in healthy cluster
test_cases.expected: Status shows node list with clear leader identification, follower count, and cluster term

test_cases.input: Check replication lag for followers
test_cases.expected: Followers show log index position relative to leader; lag visible in milliseconds

test_cases.input: Status query during leader election
test_cases.expected: Status indicates leader election in progress; no active leader ID present

test_cases.input: Status query for disconnected node
test_cases.expected: Non-responding nodes marked as unavailable in status output

scenarios.name: Backward Compatibility with Memcached Protocol
scenarios.description: Validates that existing memcached clients work unchanged with distributed MirDB cluster

steps.action: Connect existing memcached client to cluster node
steps.description: Use standard memcached client library to connect to any node
steps.context: Client should not need code changes to work with MirDB cluster

steps.description: Standard SET command should work transparently
steps.context: Client receives standard STORED response

steps.description: Standard GET should return data with standard memcached format
steps.context: Client receives VALUE response with correct data

test_cases.input: Use Python memcached client to connect to follower node and execute SET
test_cases.expected: Write succeeds (follower redirects or proxies to leader); client receives STORED response

test_cases.input: Use standard GET command with existing client
test_cases.expected: Data retrieved correctly; client can parse standard memcached response format

test_cases.input: Test all memcached commands: SET, GET, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND, DELETE
test_cases.expected: All commands behave per memcached protocol specification; responses match standard behavior

test_cases.input: Test multi-get command (GET with multiple keys)
test_cases.expected: Returns all requested values in standard memcached format

scenarios.name: Network Partition Recovery
scenarios.description: Validates that cluster correctly handles network partitions according to Raft consensus rules without data loss or split-brain scenarios

steps.description: Start 5-node cluster with stable Raft state
steps.context: Majority quorum is 3 nodes

steps.description: Disconnect network between node groups (e.g., 3 nodes vs 2 nodes)
steps.context: Partition should separate leader from minority

steps.description: Verify majority partition continues operations, minority stops
steps.context: Majority should elect new leader if leader in minority partition

steps.description: Restore network connectivity between partitions
steps.context: Cluster should reconverge and maintain consistency

test_cases.input: Partition 5-node cluster into 3-node and 2-node groups
test_cases.expected: 3-node majority continues accepting writes; 2-node minority stops; no split-brain

test_cases.input: Write succeeds in majority partition during partition; write fails in minority
test_cases.expected: Majority partition writes succeed; minority returns errors; data consistency maintained

test_cases.input: Restore network connectivity and observe cluster convergence
test_cases.expected: Nodes rejoin; cluster state converges; no data loss despite divergent operation periods

test_cases.input: Verify committed writes remain committed after partition healing
test_cases.expected: All writes committed in majority partition present after reconciliation

scenarios.name: Log Replication and Consistency Guarantees
scenarios.description: Validates that Raft log replication maintains total order and consistency across all nodes, handling sequence numbering and duplicate requests correctly

steps.description: Issue multiple SET commands to leader simultaneously
steps.context: Leader should serialize and order writes deterministically

steps.action: Verify total order in Raft logs
steps.description: Check that all followers have identical log sequences
steps.context: All committed entries should appear in same order on all nodes

steps.description: Verify applying same log entry multiple times has same result
steps.context: Log entries may be applied multiple times during leader changes

test_cases.input: Send 5 concurrent SET commands for keys A, B, C, D, E
test_cases.expected: All nodes have identical log order for entries; no logs diverge

test_cases.input: Restart leader during log replication
test_cases.expected: New leader has complete and identical log; no missing or duplicate entries

test_cases.input: Apply duplicate log entries due to leader changes
test_cases.expected: State remains consistent; duplicate application is idempotent

test_cases.input: Verify log index continuity across multiple terms
test_cases.expected: Log indices continue monotonically; no gaps or resets after leader changes

scenarios.name: Error Handling and Edge Cases
scenarios.description: Validates that cluster handles error conditions gracefully including oversized values, malformed commands, and resource exhaustion

steps.description: Attempt to store value exceeding maximum size limit
steps.context: System should return error for oversized payloads

steps.description: Send invalid protocol commands to cluster
steps.context: System should return CLIENT_ERROR without affecting cluster health

steps.description: Simulate disk exhaustion during log append or compaction
steps.context: System should fail gracefully and maintain existing data integrity

test_cases.input: SET command with 5MB value exceeding maximum size
test_cases.expected: Returns CLIENT_ERROR or appropriate error without crashing or hanging

test_cases.input: Malformed protocol: 'set key 0 0 5\r\nwrong_bytes\r\n' (only 3 bytes sent)

test_cases.input: Fill disk during Raft log append operation

steps.context: Create enough entries to trigger log compaction

steps.description: Automatic snapshot should trigger based on log size or entry count
steps.context: Snapshot captures current state machine state

steps.description: Verify old log entries are removed after snapshot creation
steps.context: Log should compact to prevent unbounded growth

steps.action: Restart node and restore from snapshot

steps.context: Node should recover efficiently using snapshot

scenarios.name: JJJ - Basic Cluster Connectivity Test
scenarios.description: Manual test scenario to verify basic cluster connectivity and node communication. This scenario validates that nodes can discover each other and establish communication channels necessary for Raft consensus operations.

steps.description: Initialize and start the first MirDB node with cluster configuration enabled
steps.context: Node should be configured with cluster membership settings and start listening for inter-node RPC connections

steps.description: Initialize and start a second MirDB node configured to join the same cluster
steps.context: Second node should attempt to discover and connect to the first node using configured peer addresses

steps.description: Check that both nodes have established communication channels with each other
steps.context: Nodes should show peer connections in status output and be ready for Raft message exchange

steps.description: Query the cluster status endpoint to confirm nodes are visible to each other
steps.context: Status should show both nodes as members of the cluster with connection state

test_cases.input: Start two nodes with matching cluster configuration and query status
test_cases.expected: Both nodes appear in cluster status as connected peers

test_cases.input: Check node logs for successful peer discovery messages
test_cases.expected: Logs show successful connection establishment between nodes

test_cases.input: Disconnect network between nodes and observe reconnection behavior
test_cases.expected: Nodes detect disconnection and automatically attempt reconnection when network is restored

explanation: This scenario tests the foundational connectivity layer required for distributed consensus
Inter-node communication is a prerequisite for all Raft operations including leader election and log replication
Validates that the gRPC/RPC transport layer functions correctly between cluster members
